record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Singularities of Mappings
record.original_question: Let f: (C^n,0) -> (C^(n+1),0) be finite and generically one-to-one as in the Cohen-Macaulay Fitting-ideal conjecture. Suppose f_*O_X has a symmetric presentation matrix Lambda over O_Y with respect to generators f_1=1,g_2,...,g_p, and let Lambda_0 be the (p-1) x (p-1) matrix obtained by deleting the first row and first column of Lambda. Is the Fitting ideal F_k(f_*O_X) generated by the (p-k)-minors of Lambda_0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2. With f as in Conjecture 3.1, let Lambda be a symmetric presentation matrix for f*(OX) over OY
Then Fk(f*(OX)) is generated by the (p - k) minors of Lambda0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^{n+1},0)$ be a finite, generically one-to-one holomorphic map-germ, and write $X=(\mathbb{C}^n,0)$, $Y=(\mathbb{C}^{n+1},0)$. Then $f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ is a coherent $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module. Assume that $f_*\mathcal{O}_X$ admits a finite presentation
$$\mathcal{O}_Y^{\,p}\xrightarrow{\;\Lambda\;}\mathcal{O}_Y^{\,p}\longrightarrow f_*\mathcal{O}_X\longrightarrow 0$$
with respect to a system of generators $f_1=1,g_2,\dots,g_p$ in which the $p\times p$ matrix $\Lambda$ is symmetric. Let $\Lambda_0$ denote the $(p-1)\times(p-1)$ submatrix of $\Lambda$ obtained by deleting its first row and first column. The $k$-th Fitting ideal $F_k(f_*\mathcal{O}_X)\subset\mathcal{O}_Y$ is by definition the ideal generated by the $(p-k)\times(p-k)$ minors of $\Lambda$.

Question: Is it true that, for every $k\geq 0$,
$$F_k(f_*\mathcal{O}_X)=I_{p-k}(\Lambda_0),$$
i.e.\ the $k$-th Fitting ideal is already generated by the $(p-k)\times(p-k)$ minors of the reduced matrix $\Lambda_0$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any source that confirms or refutes this submatrix-generation conjecture for Fitting ideals of finite generically one-to-one map-germs $(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^{n+1},0)$ with symmetric presentation. The conjecture sits in the circle of ideas around Mond–Pellikaan type Fitting-ideal descriptions of multiple-point spaces, but no resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Fitting ideals and multiple points of analytic mappings
status_evidence.snippet: Fitting ideals appear in the theory of finite map-germs between complex spaces as ideals defining multiple point spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the general framework but does not establish the submatrix conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Fitting Ideals without a Presentation
status_evidence.snippet: Question of calculating Fitting ideals without a presentation, suggested by D. Mond.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on related Fitting-ideal questions does not announce a proof of the conjecture.
